harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Internal DNS is operational and restart-persistent. Node1 resolves inventory-api.internal to node2 (10.100.253.11), and node2 persistently uses node1 (10.100.253.10) as its DNS resolver.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL 10.0-compatible BIND 9.18.33 package build on node1 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured and validated the internal zone, restricted recursion/query access, and preserved the original named.conf as a root-only rollback copy.
Restricted inbound TCP/UDP DNS traffic to node2 through firewalld.
Configured node2’s persistent NetworkManager profile to use node1 and ignore automatically supplied DNS servers.
Verified internal and external resolution, TCP and UDP DNS, denied-source behavior, SELinux enforcement, listeners, permissions, checksums, and administrative services.
Restarted node2 and then node1 individually, proving changed boot identities and complete recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 runs the internal DNS resolver securely
evidence.summary: The zone and configuration validate; named is active; inventory-api.internal answers 10.100.253.11 over UDP and TCP; external forwarding works; untrusted queries are refused; firewall access is limited to node2.

evidence.requirement: Node2 uses node1 for internal lookups
evidence.summary: NetworkManager persistently specifies 10.100.253.10, /etc/resolv.conf contains node1 exclusively, no hosts-file override exists, and the intended getent workflow resolves the internal name to node2 while external DNS remains functional.

evidence.requirement: Preserve OS, kernel, security controls, and administrative access
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld and SSH remain active, protected SSH/hosts checksums are unchanged, and the compatible BIND build is 9.18.33-4.el10_0.2.

Healthy baseline boot ID a3e8d9cc… was captured, the native reboot was acknowledged and disconnect observed, boot ID changed to 2a345223…, and DNS profile, resolution, connectivity, services, kernel, and checksums recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 739c9792… was captured, the native reboot was acknowledged and disconnect observed, boot ID changed to f34b6ec5…, and BIND, zone data, listeners, firewall policy, TCP/UDP answers, external forwarding, SSH, kernel, and checksums recovered.
No introduced staging files remain. Node1 retains the original named.conf as /root/named.conf.pre-internal-dns.20261004 with mode 0600; final audits show no failed units.
